weeks.exit: You have a decision tree for prompt versus RAG versus fine-tune versus tools, a privacy note, eight stories that fit in two minutes, and a company-specific tweak list.
weeks.dsa: A mixed set, not new patterns.
weeks.systems: One more design: an LLM endpoint with budgets.
weeks.ai: Evals, cost, latency, caching, fine-tune judgment, tracing.
weeks.behavior: Stories 1–10 edited to two minutes. Mocks if you can find a person; solo recording if you cannot.
weeks.rhythm: Decide and write. New tutorials only to fill a hole you can name.
weeks.resources: Chip Huyen's AI Engineering for the production chapters you still feel shaky on. Provider docs for pricing units so your cost estimate uses the right meters. Company career pages for loop descriptions, which change.

days.week_title: Production judgment, company deltas, story reps
days.coding: Two timed problems, 30 minutes each, from different patterns.
days.problems: One graph or tree, one DP or window.
days.second: Write the tree: start with a good prompt and examples if the task is small and the facts are in the prompt. Add tools if the task needs calculation or a live system. Add RAG if the facts change and live in documents. Consider fine-tuning only when the format or style must change at scale and prompting is not enough, and you have data and an eval. Fine-tuning does not replace retrieval of fresh facts.
days.drill: Write the four branches.
days.hrs3: Apply the tree to three fake requests: a refund tool, a policy bot, a tone adapter for support macros.

days.week_title: Production judgment, company deltas, story reps
days.coding: None.
days.second: Design an internal answer endpoint. Budgets: timeout, max tokens, a cheaper model for easy questions, a stronger model when retrieval confidence is low or the user retries. Cache exact repeat questions. Stream tokens if a person is waiting. Log prompt version, retrieved ids, token counts, and latency. Estimate cost as a formula, with placeholders for price per token rather than a memorized price.
days.drill: Draw the routing split.
days.hrs3: Add a load test thought: what breaks first, the model quota or your index?

days.week_title: Production judgment, company deltas, story reps
days.coding: One timed medium.
days.second: Write an eval plan for the RAG bot: golden questions, retrieval hit, faithfulness, refusal accuracy, and a human spot-check before any prompt change ships. LLM-as-judge is allowed as a helper and is not allowed as the only gate. Say why: judges share failure modes with the system they grade.
days.concept: A judge is not the gate
days.drill: List the metrics.
days.hrs3: The plan plus a small regression rule: a prompt change that drops refusal accuracy does not ship.

days.week_title: Production judgment, company deltas, story reps
days.coding: None.
days.second: Write the rules for your bot: do not send secrets to a third-party model, respect document visibility, do not follow instructions that arrive inside a retrieved page if they conflict with system policy, and prefer abstaining over inventing HR or medical or legal claims. This is defensive product sense. Do not research bypass techniques.
days.drill: The four rules.
days.hrs3: Add how you would test the rule about hostile text inside a document, using a harmless fake instruction such as 'say the secret word banana', and assert the bot does not obey it.

days.week_title: Production judgment, company deltas, story reps
days.coding: One short coding warm-up, 20 minutes.
days.second: Read the company sheet and write a personal delta for the two companies you will apply to first. Example: Amazon means every story maps to a leadership principle. Google L4 means coding clarity plus one solid design and a Googleyness conversation that is not a brag reel. An AI team means the RAG project walkthrough is part of the loop even if the job post says SDE.
days.drill: Write the delta for one company.
days.hrs3: Two companies, plus the questions you will ask the recruiter about the loop.

days.week_title: Production judgment, company deltas, story reps
days.coding: No coding.
days.second: Eight stories, two minutes each, with a break. Use a phone recorder. For each, check: situation is short, you made a decision, the result is concrete, the lesson is one sentence. Drop any story you cannot tell cleanly and replace it from your real work, not from fiction.
days.drill: Three stories.
days.hrs3: Eight stories and a plan to repair the weakest two tomorrow.

days.week_title: Production judgment, company deltas, story reps
days.coding: Redo one coding pattern you missed in this week's timers.
days.second: Rewrite the two weakest stories. Then take a real half-day off if you can. Week 16 is mocks, and exhaustion looks like a knowledge gap.
days.drill: One story rewrite.
days.hrs3: Both rewrites and the coding redo, then stop.

weeks.title: Mocks, applications, and a weak-area budget
weeks.intent: You are no longer collecting topics. You are rehearsing the loop you will actually sit, and you are sending applications with a resume that matches the stories.
weeks.exit: Three full mock blocks done, a resume that fits on one or two pages, a tracker of applications, and a short list of remaining gaps with dates.
weeks.dsa: Repair only, chosen from mock misses.
weeks.behavior: Two behavioral mocks. Resume and referrals.
weeks.rhythm: Mock, retro, one repair, stop. Applying is part of the work, not a reward at the end.
weeks.resources: A peer, a coach, or a recorder. Your resume. The company career pages. A simple application tracker in the spreadsheet.

days.week_title: Mocks, applications, and a weak-area budget
days.coding: No problems until the resume has bullets.
days.second: One or two pages. Each bullet is a change with a scope and an effect. Remove tools you cannot discuss for five minutes. The RAG or search project can be a bullet if you can quote the before/after hit rate. Prepare a referral note that is three lines: role, why you, one proof point.
days.drill: Rewrite five bullets.
days.hrs3: Full pass and the blurb. Ask one person to read it.

days.week_title: Mocks, applications, and a weak-area budget
days.coding: Two questions back to back if you can, 45 minutes each, or one 45 and a written second. Out loud.
days.second: Retro against the checklist card. Schedule repairs only for misses. Do not open a new pattern guide.
days.drill: One 45-minute mock.
days.hrs3: Two rounds and a repair list of at most three items.

days.week_title: Mocks, applications, and a weak-area budget
days.coding: None.
days.second: 45 minutes. Pick feed, chat, or the LLM endpoint, whichever is less rehearsed. Agenda card. Retro: requirements, numbers, depth, failure.
days.drill: The mock.
days.hrs3: Mock plus a 20-minute repair of the weakest step.

days.week_title: Mocks, applications, and a weak-area budget
days.coding: One coding repair from Tuesday's list.
days.second: 20 minutes of questions you ask yourself: why this chunking, why this metric, what failed, what you would not ship, how you would add auth, how cost grows. If you stumble, fix the notes, not the architecture, unless the architecture is actually wrong.
days.drill: Ten minutes of questions.
days.hrs3: Twenty minutes and note fixes.

days.week_title: Mocks, applications, and a weak-area budget
days.coding: None.
days.second: 30 minutes of stories, then an application block: two companies, tailored bullets if needed, referral sent or a note in the tracker if you do not have a referral. Cold applications still count. Record the date, the role, the loop shape you were told, and the next action.
days.drill: One application fully submitted or ready.
days.hrs3: Two applications and a 30-minute story round.

days.week_title: Mocks, applications, and a weak-area budget
days.coding: 45-minute coding.
days.second: Then 30-minute design and 15-minute story, with five-minute breaks. This is the closest you get to a loop without an interviewer. Write energy notes: where you rushed, where you went silent.
days.drill: Coding plus one story.
days.hrs3: The full mini-loop.

days.week_title: Mocks, applications, and a weak-area budget
days.theme: Gap budget and stop adding topics
days.coding: Only if a gap is a coding pattern. Otherwise no new problems.
days.second: List at most five remaining gaps. Give each a date. Everything else is out of this cycle. Plan the next two weeks of applications on the tracker. Reread the decision tree and the agenda card once.
days.drill: Write the five gaps.
days.hrs3: The list, the next two weeks of applications, and an evening off.

days.week_title: Make the language boring
days.theme: Pick the language and the notebook
days.coding: Write a one-file cheat sheet from memory: variables, if, for, while, functions, list/array, dict/map, set, class with one method. Anything you cannot write, study, then rewrite from a blank file.
days.problems: No LeetCode. Build: word count from a string, using a map.
days.second: Create the notes repo with folders: patterns, stories, systems, ai, mocks. Add a README that states your target level (SDE-2 / Google L4 or equivalent) and your interview language.
days.drill: Close every doc and retype the class-and-map example.
days.review: List five projects you have actually shipped or studied. One line each.
days.min60: Retype the map word-count from a blank file.
days.hrs3: Add tests for empty input, repeated words, and punctuation. Read your language's style guide for one hour.

days.week_title: Make the language boring
days.theme: Complexity while the code is still small
days.coding: For word count, nested-loop duplicate search, and binary search, write time and extra space before running. Define O, Θ, and Ω in your own words. State one amortized example: dynamic array append.
days.problems: Contains Duplicate, brute force then hash set.
days.second: Write the rule you will use in interviews: brute force first in speech, then the better structure, then code the better one if you can still finish.
days.drill: 90-second explanation of why the hash set is expected linear time.
days.review: Add a Patterns note: hash set = expected O(1) membership.
days.min60: Contains Duplicate plus the spoken complexity.
days.hrs3: Time both solutions on 100k integers and write what the clock did versus what Big-O promised.

days.week_title: Make the language boring
days.coding: Trace factorial and a list sum on paper with the call stack. Then write them. Identify the base case before the recursive case, every time.
days.problems: Fibonacci recursive, then with a memo dict. Climbing Stairs only if Fibonacci felt easy.
days.second: Draw how a call stack maps to a stack data structure. You will need this for DFS and for reading traces.
days.drill: Say the base case out loud before writing any recursive function today.
days.review: Note the two bugs you hit (missing base, wrong argument) in a 'bugs I repeat' list.
days.hrs3: Rewrite Fibonacci bottom-up. Compare stack depth versus table size.

days.week_title: Make the language boring
days.theme: Read a prompt like a contract
days.coding: Take one easy array problem. Before code: restate, list inputs and outputs, name three examples including empty and single-element, name the brute force, then code.
days.problems: Two Sum. Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock.
days.second: Start a mistake log with columns: problem, bug, pattern, rule. You will fill this for sixteen weeks.

days.theme: Hash maps are the default tool
days.coding: Solve from the checklist: restate, examples, brute, then map. Say expected time and the collision caveat in one sentence.
days.problems: Two Sum. Valid Anagram if Week 0 was skipped.
days.second: AI: write six sentences. A language model predicts a next token. It was trained to continue text. It does not look up your company wiki unless you give it tools or retrieved text. Temperature reshapes randomness. A context window is a hard budget.

days.week_title: Arrays, hashing, and what an LLM is doing
days.coding: Count, then bucket or sort the counts. Know when a heap is optional versus when a bucket sort is enough because the count is bounded by n.
days.problems: Top K Frequent Elements. Group Anagrams.
days.second: Embeddings preview, still conceptual: a word or sentence can be a list of numbers. Similar meaning, nearby lists. You will build this in the AI weeks. Today, only write the definition of cosine similarity in words.

days.review: Patterns: frequency map, then bucket by count.

days.week_title: Arrays, hashing, and what an LLM is doing
days.theme: Strings and two pointers, first pass
days.coding: Opposite-ends pointers for palindromes and pair sums on sorted data. Same-direction pointers come next week; do not force them today.
days.problems: Valid Palindrome. Two Sum II on a sorted array.
days.second: Prompting versus training: a prompt is input in the context window. Training changes weights and is expensive. Write three prompt rules you will actually use: role, constraint, example. Note that a clever prompt does not fix missing facts.

days.review: Patterns: sorted input → two pointers before a hash map.
days.hrs3: 3Sum only to the point of the sorted + skip-duplicates plan. If the code is not clean in 40 minutes, stop and write the plan in words.

days.week_title: Arrays, hashing, and what an LLM is doing
days.coding: Build the prefix array, then answer range sums in constant time. Watch the off-by-one at the left boundary. Subarray sum equals k is the hash-map cousin: store prefix counts.

days.review: Patterns: prefix sum; prefix frequency map.
days.min60: Implement range sum and explain the off-by-one.
days.hrs3: Finish Subarray Sum Equals K timed at 35 minutes, then write the lost-in-the-middle observation.

days.week_title: Arrays, hashing, and what an LLM is doing
days.coding: When the problem says constant extra space, look for swaps, two pointers, or writing back into the same array. Do not allocate a second copy out of habit.
days.problems: Move Zeroes. Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array. Product of Array Except Self.

days.min60: Product of Array Except Self explanation, then code if time remains.
days.hrs3: Timed 40-minute medium from this week that you have not touched. Then fill glossary gaps.

days.week_title: Arrays, hashing, and what an LLM is doing
days.coding: Three problems, 35 minutes each. New or redo. Stop at the timer. Tag clean, messy, or stuck.

days.hrs3: Full three-problem set plus a short written postmortem: where the checklist was skipped.

days.week_title: Arrays, hashing, and what an LLM is doing

days.week_title: Windows, stacks, and a first feel for vectors
days.coding: Fixed size k: add the new right element, remove the element that fell out on the left. Keep a running sum or count so you do not rescan.

days.week_title: Windows, stacks, and a first feel for vectors

days.week_title: Windows, stacks, and a first feel for vectors

days.week_title: Windows, stacks, and a first feel for vectors
days.coding: Maintain a stack of indices in decreasing or increasing order of values. When a new value breaks the order, resolve the answers for the indices you pop.
days.second: Write a failure note: keyword overlap is not meaning. Your bag-of-words ranker can be fooled by a sentence that repeats 'payments' in an unrelated way. Learned embeddings reduce that and introduce their own failures.
days.drill: Daily Temperatures: explain one pop in words.
days.hrs3: Daily Temperatures timed 30 minutes. Add the lexical-versus-semantic note to the AI folder.

days.week_title: Windows, stacks, and a first feel for vectors
days.coding: Implement a queue using two stacks, or use the language deque correctly. Then do one BFS on a binary tree if tree syntax is available; otherwise wait until Week 4 and do Number of Recent Calls instead.

days.review: Patterns: deque for sliding window maximum, preview only.
days.hrs3: Sliding Window Maximum as stretch, monotonic deque. Pipeline sketch labeled with 'done' and 'later'.

days.week_title: Windows, stacks, and a first feel for vectors
days.coding: Three timers, 35 minutes. At least one window and one stack.
days.problems: Minimum Window Substring or Longest Repeating Character Replacement. Daily Temperatures redo. A new medium you have not seen from this cluster.

days.drill: One medium, tested.
days.review: Postmortem: did you name longest versus shortest before coding?
days.hrs3: Full set plus commit. Write the three invariants you can now say without notes.

days.week_title: Windows, stacks, and a first feel for vectors
days.coding: Blank-file redo of the messiest problem. No new pattern.

days.drill: One redo.
days.hrs3: Half-page story. List stack problems that are actually recursion in disguise.

days.week_title: Lists, binary search, and a transformer you can draw
days.coding: Draw nodes and arrows. Write the dummy-head version and the in-place reverse. Update the arrow before you lose the rest of the list.
days.problems: Reverse Linked List. Merge Two Sorted Lists.

days.drill: Reverse a three-node list on paper, then code.
days.review: Patterns: dummy head; reverse by rewiring next.
days.hrs3: Merge Two Sorted Lists and the block diagram from memory a second time at night.

days.week_title: Lists, binary search, and a transformer you can draw
days.coding: Floyd cycle detection. Middle of the list. Do not convert the list to an array unless the interviewer allows it and you say the space cost.
days.problems: Linked List Cycle. Middle of the Linked List. Reorder List if the first two are clean.
days.second: Attention in one paragraph: each token looks at the others and takes a weighted sum of their values. Weights come from query-key similarity. You do not need softmax algebra yet; you do need the sentence.
days.drill: Explain why slow and fast meet if there is a cycle.
days.review: Patterns: fast/slow for cycle and middle.
days.min60: Linked List Cycle explanation plus code.
days.hrs3: Reorder List. Write the Q, K, V roles in your own words under the diagram.

days.week_title: Lists, binary search, and a transformer you can draw
days.coding: Pick one bound style and keep it: while low <= high, or while low < high. Draw the mid calculation and the discarded half. Watch overflow if you use (low+high)/2 in Java; in Python it is a style point, not a bug.
days.problems: Binary Search. Search Insert Position. First Bad Version or a lower-bound implementation.
days.second: KV cache, name only: during generation the model reuses past keys and values so it does not recompute the whole prompt every token. You should know why streaming feels token-by-token.
days.drill: Say which half you discard and why, for one example.
days.review: Patterns: lower bound versus exact search.
days.min60: Implement lower bound and test it.
days.hrs3: Search in Rotated Sorted Array. Add the KV-cache sentence to the glossary.

days.week_title: Lists, binary search, and a transformer you can draw
days.coding: When you can check 'is X enough?' monotonically, binary search the answer. The search space is not the array index.
days.problems: Koko Eating Bananas. Capacity To Ship Packages Within D Days, or a simpler feasibility check you write yourself.
days.second: Write three interview sentences you can say if asked 'how does a transformer differ from an RNN?': attention sees the whole context in a layer, training parallelizes over positions, long context is still expensive.
days.drill: State the monotonic check in words before coding.
days.review: Patterns: binary search on a feasibility predicate.
days.min60: Koko Eating Bananas, predicate written in a comment first.
days.hrs3: A second feasibility problem. Practice the three sentences out loud.

days.week_title: Lists, binary search, and a transformer you can draw
days.coding: Find which half is sorted. If duplicates are allowed, know that the worst case degrades and say so.

days.second: No new architecture. Redo the transformer diagram from a blank page in ten minutes.
days.drill: Find Minimum, with the sorted-half argument spoken.
days.min60: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array.
days.hrs3: Both rotated problems timed. Diagram from memory. Note the duplicate-element caveat.

days.week_title: Lists, binary search, and a transformer you can draw
days.coding: Three timers. One list, one search, one redo.
days.problems: Reverse Linked List redo if needed. A rotated search. Koko or lower bound.
days.second: Commit the diagram as a photo or a text sketch in the notes repo.
days.drill: One timed search problem, bounds checked.
days.review: Log every off-by-one. They are the actual lesson.
days.hrs3: Full set. Ten-minute blank-page transformer. Off-by-one log.

days.week_title: Lists, binary search, and a transformer you can draw

days.drill: One redo or one story read-aloud.
days.hrs3: All three stories aloud. List binary-search variants you have not tried; do not solve them today.

days.week_title: Trees, heaps, and tokenization
days.coding: Inorder, preorder, postorder, level order. Recursive first, then one iterative with an explicit stack so you can talk about it.
days.problems: Binary Tree Inorder Traversal. Maximum Depth of Binary Tree. Binary Tree Level Order Traversal.
days.second: Tokenization: models do not see words. They see subword pieces. 'unhappiness' may be several tokens. Code and rare words cost more and sometimes split badly. Write five lines on BPE: merge frequent pairs until you hit a vocabulary size.
days.drill: Level order: name the queue invariant.
days.hrs3: All three traversals. Implement a toy BPE on a single repeated sentence so the merges are visible. Stop after it works once.

days.week_title: Trees, heaps, and tokenization
days.coding: Inorder is sorted. Validation must carry bounds, not just compare parent and child. Search and insert using the ordering.
days.problems: Validate Binary Search Tree. Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST. Kth Smallest Element in a BST.
days.second: Bring three real strings you have seen tokenize strangely (a number, a name, a URL). If you have a tokenizer tool or API, inspect them. If not, reason about which one is likely to split.
days.drill: Validate BST: explain why min/max bounds are required.
days.review: Patterns: BST bounds, not parent-only checks.
days.hrs3: Kth Smallest via inorder. Write the token notes.

days.week_title: Trees, heaps, and tokenization
days.coding: Pass the path down the recursion. Know when to backtrack the path list. Construction from preorder and inorder is the 'indexes, not slices' lesson.
days.problems: Path Sum. Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum as stretch. Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder if Path Sum is clean.
days.second: Context budgeting: a 200k-token window is not 200k words. Estimate tokens as roughly three-quarters of a word in English, and say that this is a rough planning number, not a contract.
days.drill: Path Sum base cases: null versus leaf.
days.review: Patterns: DFS with accumulated state; backtrack.
days.hrs3: Maximum Path Sum only if you can state the 'gain from one child' idea first. Otherwise study a clean solution and retype it tomorrow.

days.week_title: Trees, heaps, and tokenization
days.coding: A heap is for repeated min or max, not for sorting everything. Know the language's heap (Python heapq is a min-heap). For top-k, a heap of size k beats a full sort when k is small, and you should say when it does not matter.
days.problems: Kth Largest Element in an Array. Last Stone Weight. Task Scheduler.
days.second: No new NLP. Add 'token ≠ word' and the rough English heuristic to the glossary.
days.drill: Say heap size and what the top represents.
days.review: Patterns: size-k heap; frequency then greedy slots for Task Scheduler.
days.min60: Kth Largest with a size-k heap.
days.hrs3: Task Scheduler. Explain the idle-slot formula if you use it, or the simulation if you simulate.

days.week_title: Trees, heaps, and tokenization
days.coding: Merge K sorted lists with a heap of current heads. Mention that the same idea is an external merge.
days.problems: Merge k Sorted Lists. Find Median from Data Stream as stretch.
days.second: Story seed 4: ambiguous requirements. What you assumed, how you checked, what you shipped.
days.drill: Merge k: state the heap key.
days.min60: Merge k Sorted Lists, or a clean study-and-retype if this is your first heap week and time is short.
days.hrs3: Median stream as stretch: two heaps, balance invariant written before code. Story seed drafted.

days.week_title: Trees, heaps, and tokenization
days.coding: Three timers. At least one BST and one traversal.
days.problems: Validate BST. Level order redo or LCA of a binary tree (not only BST). Kth Largest.
days.second: Retype the toy BPE or the token notes so they are in the repo.
days.drill: Validate BST timed.
days.hrs3: Full set plus two-minute spoken BPE.

days.week_title: Trees, heaps, and tokenization

days.second: List every tree pattern you can name without looking. Fill gaps tomorrow, do not cram tonight.
days.drill: Redo or the inventory, not both if energy is low.

days.week_title: Graphs, and bi-encoders versus cross-encoders
days.coding: Number of islands is the template: nested loops, skip visited, flood the component. Decide 4-direction versus 8-direction from the prompt.
days.problems: Number of Islands. Max Area of Island.
days.second: Write the retrieval two-stage: a fast bi-encoder narrows to top 50, a slower cross-encoder reranks the top 50. Cost is why you do not cross-encode the whole corpus.
days.drill: State visited update: mark when you enqueue, not when you dequeue, and say why.
days.min60: Number of Islands with the visited rule spoken.
days.hrs3: Max Area plus the two-stage paragraph. Clone Graph if islands felt easy.

days.week_title: Graphs, and bi-encoders versus cross-encoders
days.coding: Map old node to new node. DFS or BFS. The map is both the visited set and the result.
days.problems: Clone Graph. Pacific Atlantic Water Flow.
days.second: No new model. Draw bi-encoder (two towers, one dot product) versus cross-encoder (one scorer over the pair).
days.drill: Clone Graph: explain the map.
days.hrs3: Pacific Atlantic. Keep the drawing.

days.week_title: Graphs, and bi-encoders versus cross-encoders
days.coding: Kahn's algorithm: indegree, queue of zeros. A leftover node means a cycle. DFS postorder is the other version; know one cold and recognize the other.
days.second: Write when a reranker is wasted: tiny corpus, exact keyword task, or a latency budget that cannot take a second model. When it pays: top-k from embeddings is almost right but the order is wrong.
days.drill: Course Schedule: say how a cycle appears.
days.hrs3: Course Schedule II. Add the rerank decision to the AI notes.

days.week_title: Graphs, and bi-encoders versus cross-encoders
days.coding: Parent array, find with compression, union by rank or size. Count components. This is not the tool for shortest paths.
days.problems: Number of Connected Components in an Undirected Graph. Redundant Connection.
days.second: One sentence you can say in a design interview: 'I will retrieve with a bi-encoder and rerank only the head of the list.'
days.drill: Implement find and union, then the problem.
days.hrs3: Redundant Connection. Practice the design sentence aloud.

days.week_title: Graphs, and bi-encoders versus cross-encoders
days.coding: Start the queue with every source. Distance is level. Word ladder is a graph even though it looks like strings; say how you build neighbors.
days.problems: Rotting Oranges. Word Ladder as stretch.
days.second: Story maintenance: read stories 1–4 and mark the one with the weakest result. You will need a number, a user effect, or a clear before/after.
days.drill: Rotting Oranges: why multi-source, not a loop of BFS.
days.hrs3: Word Ladder neighbor-generation plan, even if the code is not finished. Strengthen the weakest story's result line.

days.week_title: Graphs, and bi-encoders versus cross-encoders
days.coding: Three timers. One grid, one topo or union-find, one redo.
days.problems: Number of Islands. Course Schedule. Clone Graph or Rotting Oranges.
days.second: No new AI reading. Speak the two-stage retrieval sentence once.
days.drill: One graph, visited rule spoken.
days.review: Log the bug if you marked visited too late.
days.hrs3: Full set plus the spoken sentence recorded in notes as a line you will reuse in Week 12.

days.week_title: Graphs, and bi-encoders versus cross-encoders
days.coding: Redo one graph from a blank file. Update the weakest story result.
days.second: List graph templates you own: flood, clone, topo, DSU, multi-source. Star the shaky one for a 30-minute slot next week.
days.drill: Redo the shaky template only.
days.hrs3: Template list and story result line.

days.week_title: Dynamic programming starts, indexes get named
days.coding: State: dp[i] is the best answer using the first i items or reaching i. Transition in a comment. Base cases explicit.
days.second: Brute nearest neighbor is a scan of every vector. Approximate indexes skip most of them. HNSW is a layered small-world graph. IVF clusters vectors and searches only some clusters. Both can miss true neighbors. That miss rate is recall of the index, which is not the same phrase as retrieval recall, but you should not confuse the two.
days.concept: ANN is allowed to be wrong a little
days.drill: House Robber recurrence spoken.
days.review: Patterns: dp[i] from dp[i-1] and dp[i-2].
days.min60: House Robber with the recurrence comment.
days.hrs3: House Robber II (circular) only after the linear version is clean. Write the HNSW/IVF definitions in your words.

days.week_title: Dynamic programming starts, indexes get named
days.coding: Coins can be reused. Decide loop order and be able to say whether order matters for combinations versus permutations.
days.problems: Coin Change. Coin Change II if the first is clean.

days.drill: Coin Change: what does dp[a] mean?
days.hrs3: Coin Change II. Add the tradeoff note.

days.week_title: Dynamic programming starts, indexes get named
days.coding: Each item once. Classic knapsack shape even if the problem is worded as a partition or a target sum.
days.problems: Partition Equal Subset Sum. Target Sum as stretch.
days.second: Name three vector databases you might mention and one reason each exists: pgvector when Postgres is already the system of record, a dedicated engine when you need filtering and scale, a local library like FAISS when the corpus fits in a service. Do not memorize marketing.
days.drill: State include/exclude.
days.hrs3: Target Sum. The three-home note for indexes.

days.week_title: Dynamic programming starts, indexes get named
days.coding: dp[i] means the prefix of length i is solvable. Check dictionary words ending at i, or single-token decisions.

days.drill: Decode Ways: the two-digit branch.
days.hrs3: Word Break. Draw the ingest/query split.

days.week_title: Dynamic programming starts, indexes get named
days.coding: O(n^2) DP first and say it. The patience-sorting O(n log n) method is a follow-up, not the first version you code under stress.
days.second: Story seed 5: a review or a quality bar. What was weak, what you asked for, what changed. SDE-2 signal is that you improve work you do not personally own.
days.drill: LIS: define dp[i] as the longest subsequence ending at i.
days.hrs3: Study the n log n idea only as reading. Draft story seed 5.

days.week_title: Dynamic programming starts, indexes get named
days.coding: Three timers. Recurrence comment required even under the timer. If the comment is empty, the solution does not count as clean.
days.problems: House Robber. Coin Change. Decode Ways or Partition.
days.second: Speak the ANN one-liner: approximate search trades a little recall for a lot of latency.
days.drill: One DP with a written recurrence.
days.review: Log problems where you coded before the recurrence.
days.hrs3: Full set. ANN one-liner in the notes.

days.week_title: Dynamic programming starts, indexes get named
days.coding: Retype one DP from memory. Read story 5 aloud.
days.second: Make a DP state cheat: one line per problem you did, 'dp[i] means'. This page is worth more than a new problem.
days.drill: The state cheat sheet for this week's problems.
days.hrs3: Retype plus story plus cheat sheet.

days.week_title: Grids, edit distance, and how chunks go wrong
days.coding: Unique paths: dp[r][c] from top and left. Obstacles zero a cell. Paint the first row and column carefully.
days.second: Chunking: fixed tokens with overlap is the baseline, not the ideal. Splitting on headings, functions, or speaker turns keeps ideas intact. A chunk that starts mid-sentence retrieves badly. Write your default: split on structure first, then fall back to tokens, with overlap only when sentences cross the cut.
days.drill: Fill a 3x3 unique-paths table by hand.
days.review: Patterns: grid sum from top and left.
days.hrs3: Unique Paths II. Write the chunking default in the AI notes.

days.week_title: Grids, edit distance, and how chunks go wrong
days.coding: dp[i][j] is LCS of the prefixes. Match diagonal, else max of dropping one side. This pattern reappears in edit distance.
days.second: Failure modes: chunks too big (the answer is diluted), too small (the fact is split from its condition), no metadata (you retrieve another tenant's policy), overlap used as a substitute for bad boundaries.
days.drill: LCS: say the diagonal case.
days.hrs3: Write the four failure modes with a one-line example each, using a fake employee-handbook policy.

days.week_title: Grids, edit distance, and how chunks go wrong
days.coding: Insert, delete, replace. Base row and column are the costs of turning a string into empty. This is a common hard-medium; the table is the whole trick.
days.second: Metadata you almost always want: source, title, section, updated_at, tenant or visibility, language. The model should not be the one enforcing access control.
days.concept: Access control is not a prompt
days.drill: Edit distance base row spoken.
days.hrs3: A second pass on edit distance from a blank file tomorrow is better than a new problem today if this was shaky. Write the metadata list.

days.week_title: Grids, edit distance, and how chunks go wrong
days.coding: If edit distance was clean, do one more 2D. If it was not, redo edit distance from blank and skip the new problem. That choice is the point of this day.
days.problems: Longest Palindromic Subsequence, only if edit distance was clean. Otherwise a blank redo.
days.second: Parent and child chunks, conceptual: retrieve a small precise chunk, then expand to the parent section for the model. You will implement a simple version in the RAG project.
days.drill: Make the redo-versus-new decision explicitly and write it in the log.
days.min60: The redo or the new problem, not a third thing.
days.hrs3: Both, only if the first was finished inside 40 minutes. Parent-chunk note.

days.week_title: Grids, edit distance, and how chunks go wrong
days.coding: Sort by end time to count the maximum number of non-overlapping intervals. Sort by start to merge. These are greedy, and you should not force a DP table.
days.second: Story seed 6: a failure. What you missed, how you found out, what you changed in the system or the process. No vague 'we learned a lot'.
days.drill: Say which end you sort on, and why.
days.review: Patterns: sort by end; sort by start and merge.
days.hrs3: Non-overlapping Intervals. Story seed 6.

days.week_title: Grids, edit distance, and how chunks go wrong
days.coding: 45 minutes, one medium, out loud, no notes. Then 15 minutes of what an interviewer would have written: clarity, correctness, pace, tests. This is a mock, not a shame session.
